newsitem.title: USA: Idaho Power predicts heavy spring runoff.
newsitem.headline: Idaho Power predicts heavy spring runoff.

text.p: Idaho Power expects spring runoff this year to be well above average, based on weather forecasts, above normal snowpack conditions and carryover reservoir storage, the utility said this week in a newsletter.
The flows are expected to translate into above-normal hydroelectric generation, typically the lowest-cost source of power.
Inflows into the utility's Brownlee Reservoir on the Snake River were predicted to total 11 million acre feet (maf) for April to July, compared with an above-average 8.3 maf last year.
The 66-year median inflow to Brownlee is 4.81 maf.
"Extremely wet conditions coupled with cold temperatures increased snowpack at all elevations in mid-December," said Idaho Power hydrologic engineer Nengjin Liu.
He noted wet, warm weather in late December melted some low-level snowpack, but higher elevation snowpack continued to build.
For the Snake River above Brownlee, the early January weighted average snow water equivalent was 219 percent of the 30-year average, compared with 104 percent last year at this time.
On January 1, total storage for selected reservoirs above Brownlee was 5.69 maf, which was 78 percent of capacity and 124 percent of average.
